options.text: The population loss was caused entirely by Spanish armies in battle.

options.text: Disease caused a demographic catastrophe across the Americas in the 1500s.
Native populations grew steadily throughout the 1500s and 1600s.
options.misconception: The table shows collapse, not growth, in every row.

rationales.general:
1. Read each row. Hispaniola lost nearly everyone; half to nine-tenths of the Americas died; smallpox hit Mexico.
2. Ask what the rows share. Every row is a population falling to disease.
3. Check the scale. The loss spans islands and mainlands over more than a century.
4. Rule out the rest. Nothing grows, smallpox reached Mexico, and battles are not in the table.
Remember: when a table shows the same pattern in every row, name the pattern.
rationales.C: Every row shows a population falling to disease: Hispaniola nearly emptied, half to nine-tenths of the Americas dead, smallpox in Mexico.

stimulus.source_note: Data table drawn from Barron's Premium 2027 Chapter 3, 'Disease and Death', and 5 Steps to a 5 2024 Chapter 6.
stimulus.text:
| Place and time | What happened |
| Hispaniola, 1492 to the 1540s | Native population fell from over 1,000,000 to about 500 |
| The Americas, 1500 to 1650 | Between 50 and 90 percent of Native peoples died |
| Mexico, 1520 to 1530 | Smallpox epidemic devastated Native populations |
